messages:
maria: noticing a bunch of logs in Kibana where trace_id and request_id are missing if the message has a prefix like \"user-pref:...\". only shows up if we search by literal prefix. filing here before morning. anyone seen this?

ops-bot: ALERT: loki_ingest_error_rate > 5% for tenant=prod (5m) :rotating_light:

aj: can you paste an example query + a raw log line?

maria: sure. in Kibana I run: `message: \"user-pref:abc123\"` and see entries with no `trace_id`. when I run `message: \"abc123\"` the trace_id appears. sample raw line: 
```
user-pref:abc123 service=api host=api-12 msg=\"request processed\" status=200
// expected metadata: trace_id=3f9a..., request_id=hdr-77
```

kai: interesting. sounds like something upstream is stripping fields when a prefix token is present. could be our vector/ingest pipeline doing prefix-splitting or kv cache key normalization.

aj: running a quick Loki query to compare:
```
{job=\"ingester\"} |= \"user-pref:abc123\" | json
```
returns the raw line with no trace field.

aj: pulled last 200 lines from vector on api-12: run:
```
kubectl logs -n infra vector-api-12 -c vector --tail 200 | tail -n 80
```
found these two entries showing `json_parse_error` and `fields_collapsed` warnings.

maria: here's the vector transform block we ship in prod (snippet):
```
[sources.kafka]
[sinks.loki]
  inputs = [\"kafka\"]
  encoding.codec = \"json\"
  [transforms.strip_prefix]
    type = \"remap\"
    source = \"parse_regex!(.message, /^(?P<prefix>[^ ]+):(?P<body>.*)$/)\"
    # config that was intended to remove noisy prefixes
    request_prefix_strip = true
```

kai: ah. `request_prefix_strip = true` was added last month to shrink cache key cardinality. it may be mutating the message before json extraction so `trace_id` ends up in a different field or dropped.

aj: can we confirm by querying raw bytes from Kafka for the same message id?

maria: I pulled the kafka payload for the sample offset: shows `trace_id` in the payload, so it exists pre-ingest. payload: `{"msg":"user-pref:abc123 ...","trace_id":"3f9a..."}`

kai: ok that points to the transform. quick workaround: set `request_prefix_strip = false` in the loki/ingest transform and roll to canary for api-12 only. low risk.

eng-runtime: pinging runtime infra — can we flip the env flag on the transform for canary?

sre-oncall: scope/impact? are we changing behavior that affects SLOs or cost?

kai: impact: cache key cardinality increases slightly for a subset of messages. cost delta expected <0.4% from estimates. SLO: avoids losing trace linking which matters for oncall.

aj: prepared a one-liner to find affected tenants across hot days:
```
loki -q '{job=\"ingester\"} |= \"user-pref:\" | json | __error__!="" | count_over_time(1h)
```
returns ~8k hits in last 24h concentrated on api-12 and api-09.

maria: rolling this to canary now on api-12. will monitor for new `fields_collapsed` warnings and trace reappearance.

ops-bot: DEPLOY STARTED: vector-transform/api-12 @maria (1870345740)

aj: also adding a Kibana saved search to detect \"message has prefix but missing trace_id\" so we catch regressions. query: `message: \"*:*\" AND NOT trace_id:*`

maria: can see traces reappearing in Kibana for sample queries after deploy. preliminary: trace_id visible again for `user-pref:*` messages.

sre-oncall: good. can we document the change and add a regression test?

kai: yes — I'll add a unit test on the transform that ensures `trace_id` survives prefix-remap and an integration check in our ingest e2e job. will open a PR.

eng-runtime: noted. we'll schedule a follow-up to consider smarter cache key bucketing that preserves context while controlling cardinality.

maria: thanks all. followup: add a Grafana panel to show \"prefix-messages lacking trace_id\" trend and alert if >1% of those messages miss trace for >10m.

aj: created ticket: INF-3427 to track the dashboard + PR linking. tagging `eng-runtime` for next-week deep-dive. :+1: 

ops-bot: DEPLOY SUCCESS: vector-transform/api-12 (1870345842)

maria: closing thread — we'll keep monitoring and discuss in standup. thanks. :slightly_smiling_face:
